sources.summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (HTTP 401 paywall); the underlying source is a Reuters report (August 2022) on Indonesian police denying violence in the death of a transgender rights activist who died in police custody in Bali after an arrest on drug charges.

The Harvard Crimson (1 September 2022): the mother of Rodrigo Ventocilla, a 32-year-old Peruvian transgender man who co-founded a Lima trans-rights group and studied at the Harvard Kennedy School, alleges he was beaten by police and received inadequate medical care before dying in a Denpasar hospital while still in police custody, days after being arrested for marijuana possession at Bali's airport on his honeymoon; the family alleges extortion demands rising from $100,000 to $200,000, claims the arrest was motivated by racism and transphobia, and says they hold evidence of torture, disputing the official account.

The Diplomat feature (14 August 2026) on Indonesia's trans community facing growing repression: President Prabowo Subianto's October 2025 presidential decree listed "the promotion of LGBTQ+ culture" among nonmilitary security threats alongside terrorism and drugs; a wave of vigilante mob attacks on trans women during 14-16 July 2026, including in West Java's Bogor, followed, as the government moves to codify anti-LGBTQ+ attitudes into law.
